Which object is worth fixing

Shallow size

  • Memory the object holds itself
  • Often small

Retained size

  • Memory freed by deleting the object
  • Includes what only it keeps alive

Retained size tells you which object is worth fixing.

When you do not know the action

Start recordingAllocation Timeline
Blue barnew memory allocated
Zoom on the barConstructor pane filters to it
Read Retainerssame as with snapshots

A leak is memory that stays after you undo an action.

Two heap snapshots show it.

Take Snapshot 1.

Do the suspect action, then undo it, a few times.

Take Snapshot 2 and open the Comparison view.

Each snapshot starts with a garbage collection, so only reachable objects stay.

Objects added after the undo should be gone.

If they are still there, something holds them.

Select the added object.

The Retainers section lists who points to it.

Here a JavaScript variable still holds a list that the page removed,

so it is a Detached ul.

Shallow size is the memory the object holds itself.

Retained size is what you free by deleting it.

A small object can retain a lot.

Clear the variable that holds the list.

Repeat the action and undo, take a new snapshot,

and the Detached ul is gone.

The Allocation Timeline records new memory over time.

Each blue bar is a candidate leak.

Zoom on a bar to see what was allocated then.
